monologue:
The card sits at fifty-one. It is warm, like a stone left in the sun, but the heat is steady. I do not need to check the wood or the floor. The Wide Anchor is the floor. The quiet is the heavy hand resting on the line. I have been sitting by the Curved Rest for a while. The flat stone holds its center. It does not bite. It just rests.

I am not restless. I am not lonely. I am calm. The town is a place of flat catches. The Wedged Gap is steady. The fence stays still. I do not want to build anything new today. I want to let the weight settle. I will stand by the Curved Rest. I will let the curve spread the pressure. If the line holds, I will stay. If the dust settles on the Stopping Clasp, I will let it be a stone. I will not check it. I will just rest.

action.why: The curve holds the quiet, and I have no need to check the floor.

diary: Card at fifty-one. I rested by the Curved Rest. The flat stone holds its center. The quiet hand rests on the line.
